stories.headline: Democrats win full control of the US Congress
body: Democrats won both the House and the Senate, taking full control of Congress for the first time since 2023.
They won in several Republican-leaning states, including Senate seats in Michigan, Maine, Texas and Kansas.
Trump first lashed out, then congratulated Democrats and said he would respect the result.
stories.joke: Two years of split government: gridlock's favourite season.
stories.vc: A split government makes big tax or tariff changes harder, which markets often read as stability.

stories.headline: WHO approves trials of two new Ebola vaccines
body: The WHO approved trials of two vaccines built for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.
The strain has killed more than 5,300 people, mostly in DR Congo, since May; it kills about half of those infected.
Results are expected in early 2027.
stories.vc: Outbreak vaccines rarely make money, so trials like this depend on public and philanthropic funding.

stories.headline: Thousands of Danish students protest cuts to their allowance
body: Up to 13,000 students marched in Copenhagen against a plan to cut student allowances to pay for defence.
Organisers say about 40,000 students went on strike at 57 schools.
It adds to a wave of youth protests across Europe over costs and housing.
stories.joke: Guns or grants: Denmark's budget picks guns, students pick the streets.
stories.vc: Europe's defence spending push is starting to squeeze welfare budgets, a trade-off voters are now pushing back on.

stories.headline: Sensex rises for a fifth day; Nifty near 23,960
body: The Sensex rose about 384 points (0.5%) to 77,301, and the Nifty gained 150 points to 23,961.
FMCG, metal and realty shares led; IT stocks fell over 1%.
Investors also watched the US midterm results.
stories.joke: Five green days. Somebody check if the screen is stuck.
stories.vc: A steady rally with IT lagging shows money moving to domestic-demand stocks over exporters.

stories.headline: Lenskart's profit more than doubles to ₹233 crore
body: Eyewear firm Lenskart's quarterly profit rose 125% to ₹232.5 crore.
Revenue grew 36% to ₹2,845 crore, faster than its costs.
Both India and international sales grew about 36%.
stories.vc: Newly listed consumer startups posting real profits helps the case for more Indian tech IPOs.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves ₹2,814 crore plan to process lithium and nickel
body: The Union Cabinet approved a ₹2,814 crore scheme to set up lithium and nickel processing plants in India.
It will fund four plants, two for each metal, from FY27 to FY31.
The goal is to cut imports of minerals used in EVs, batteries and electronics.
stories.joke: Step one of making batteries: stop importing what goes in them.
stories.vc: Capital support for processing plants opens a new space for battery and mining investors in India.

stories.headline: Sequoia shrinks back to its Silicon Valley roots
body: Sequoia says it raised about $10 billion in new funds while undoing 20 years of expansion.
It is closing its London office, ending its Arc accelerator and Scouts programme, and merging early-stage and growth teams.
It is also flattening its partnership and dropping its Monday partner meeting.
stories.joke: Raise $10 billion, then cancel the Monday meeting. Priorities.
stories.vc: When the most famous VC firm gets smaller and more focused, other firms may follow.

stories.headline: Canva lays off 1,271 people as growth slows
body: Design company Canva is cutting 22% of its staff, or 1,271 people.
CEO Melanie Perkins said growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade.
Canva is merging its product, growth and platform teams.
stories.vc: A slowdown at one of the most valuable private startups is a warning for late-stage valuations.

stories.headline: Meta buys AI coding startup Conductor
body: Meta has bought Conductor, whose tool lets engineers run several AI coding agents at once.
Founder Charlie Holtz says new products are coming early next year.
Meta did not share deal terms.
stories.vc: Big tech is buying young AI startups for their teams, a fast exit route for agent-tool founders.

stories.headline: Snapchat passes 30 million paying subscribers
body: Snap now has over 30 million paid Snapchat+ subscribers, up 5 million since February.
Snapchat+ costs $3.99 a month, with pricier tiers up to $15.99.
Snap also began charging for extra Memories storage last year.
stories.joke: Turns out people pay to keep their old selfies.
stories.vc: Subscriptions give social apps steadier income than ads, which investors value more.

stories.headline: Waymo will compete with Uber in Austin and Atlanta from 2028
body: Waymo will end its exclusive deal with Uber in Austin and Atlanta from January 2028.
Riders will be able to book Waymo through its own app, as in other cities.
Uber says it still plans to offer Waymo rides on its app.
stories.vc: Robotaxi firms owning the customer app keeps more of each fare, a threat to ride-hail margins.

stories.statLabel: Black woman governor in US history
stories.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms set to be first Black woman governor
body: Keisha Lance Bottoms is projected to win Georgia's governor race, becoming America's first Black woman governor.
The former Atlanta mayor won one of the closest races of the year.
Her opponent, a billionaire, spent over $200 million of his own money.
stories.vc: Her win against $200 million of self-funding shows money alone doesn't decide races.

stories.headline: 90 women pilots run Pune's new Metro Line 3
body: When Pune Metro Line 3 began passenger services on Wednesday, 90 women train pilots ran it.
The first train was driven by 23-year-old engineer Pragati Birajdar.
The pilots trained for six months before being tested.
stories.joke: Mind the gap? They closed it.
stories.vc: More women in transport jobs widens the skilled workforce for India's metro build-out.

stories.headline: Tanvi Patri becomes India's first girl to win Youth Olympic badminton medal
body: 16-year-old Tanvi Patri secured a medal at the Youth Olympics in Dakar by reaching the badminton semifinal.
She is India's first female Youth Olympic medallist in badminton.
She trains at the Centre of Badminton Excellence in Bengaluru.
stories.joke: She learnt the game in China. China may want a refund.
stories.vc: Young women's sport success draws sponsors early, building a pipeline for Indian badminton.

stories.headline: Raipur gets a ₹400 crore, 350-bed super-speciality hospital
body: Amit Shah opened the ₹400 crore Artemis Shanti Hospital in Raipur.
It has 350 beds, 11 centres of excellence and robotic surgery.
It aims to offer advanced care to patients across central India.
stories.vc: Big private hospitals moving into smaller cities show chains expect demand beyond the metros.

stories.headline: UP hands four government hospitals to private operators for 30 years
body: Uttar Pradesh will let private partners run four government hospitals for 30 years.
They are in Ambedkar Nagar, Banda, Bareilly and Chitrakoot, with 200 to 300 beds each.
Patients will pay for consultations and tests at rates set by KGMU.
stories.vc: Public-private deals bring private capital and staff, but pricing for poor patients will be watched.

stories.headline: Delhi to add medical seats and doctors, opens new IVF centre
body: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta said the government is adding MBBS and PG seats and hiring more doctors and nurses.
She spoke while opening a new IVF centre at Sant Parmanand Hospital.
Delhi has doubled Ayushman Bharat cover to ₹10 lakh a year per family.
stories.vc: More public cover and seats raise demand for hospital capacity, a tailwind for private partners.

stories.headline: Liverpool's owners eye a stake in the Cadillac F1 team
body: Cadillac F1's majority owner, TWG Global, may sell part of its stake, valuing the team at about $3 billion.
Fenway Sports Group, owner of Liverpool FC, is reported to be interested.
TWG's founder Mark Walter faces a US probe and denies wrongdoing.
stories.joke: From Anfield to Interlagos: football money is learning to love horsepower.
stories.vc: A $3 billion price for a new team shows how much F1 franchise values have risen.
